analysis:
All four units are documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md (head excerpts, lines 1634-2316) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a date bump, a schema-5 benchmark note, and a new env-var row). No code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, App Attest or cache-crypto behavior changes. I checked the changed text against the threat model.

The new invariants 8 and 9 (inference.md lines 2030-2047) and the table rows for prefill geometry describe operational scheduler geometry (prefill chunk, step budget, solo stripe, media chunk ceiling, Gemma 4 block size). This touches availability and memory admission (TB-007, T-029) but only documents behavior. The documented 1,120-token floor and 512-token bidirectional media ceiling read as bounds, not relaxations. The docs state that admission, KV budget and memory checks remain mandatory.

The new env knobs DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS (cli-reference.md line 1755) are operator-local controls on the provider host. The operator is already the adversary for local state (TB-003), so they add no new trust boundary. Whether the code clamps overrides against the Gemma 4 block minimum cannot be verified from the supplied docs. The text says chunk overrides are raised to 1,120, and the implementation is outside the supplied evidence.

The cache-related text (prefix reuse, SSD checkpoints, media noncacheable) is consistent with T-041 and adds no new at-rest artifacts. The statements that media stays noncacheable and that the paged and encrypted-restart gates remain unqualified are conservative. The text says the benchmark records scheduler geometry and fails on mismatch, which is an integrity-positive note. No threat-model update is needed, except that T-041 affected_files could later track prefix/paging docs if code changes accompany them. Code-level verification of the documented claims belongs to the code units of this PR, which are not in this batch.
